caption:
OpenAI is in talks to hand its shelved video model Sora to a startup building AI tools for filmmakers, The Information reported.

The startup's co-founders include Hollywood mogul Jeffrey Katzenberg and former Sora research lead Bill Peebles. OpenAI could get an equity stake if a deal closes.

Would you pay for a pro version of Sora?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: PYMNTS

slides.headline: OpenAI is reportedly bringing *Sora* back from the dead, with a Hollywood twist

image.generate: Vertical photo inside a dark, empty Hollywood film soundstage. In the center, a large vintage cinema camera on a tripod is half covered by a dusty white sheet, and a sleek white robotic hand is pulling the sheet off, as if waking the camera up after a long sleep. A single hard spotlight from above lights the camera and the hand; dust floats in the beam. The screen of the phone app in the first image is reflected faintly in the camera lens. The camera and hand fill the upper two thirds of the frame with headroom above; the left third of the frame is empty dark background; the bottom third is a dark concrete studio floor. Blank surfaces, no readable text or labels on any object, no letters, no watermarks. Photorealistic, high contrast, one clear subject. It must look like an unedited real photo from a news agency, not a painting, not digital art, no glow effects.

slides.heading: A *second act*
paras: OpenAI is in talks to hand Sora to a startup building AI video tools for filmmakers, The Information reported on Monday.
The startup wants to improve Sora and sell software and services built on it. No deal has been finalized.

slides.heading: The *Hollywood* founders
paras: The unnamed startup's co-founders are Hollywood mogul Jeffrey Katzenberg, former Sora research lead Bill Peebles and former Dropbox CFO Sujay Jaswa.
Katzenberg and Jaswa also co-founded the tech investment firm WndrCo, according to their LinkedIn profiles.

slides.heading: Weights on *the table*?
paras: It is unclear whether OpenAI would share Sora's model weights. A source told The Information the startup would get enough access to substantially customize it.
If the deal closes, OpenAI would reportedly receive an equity stake.

slides.heading: Why Sora *went dark*
paras: OpenAI announced in March that it was discontinuing Sora. The model reportedly needed huge computing power while its revenue stayed limited.

paras.t: If it returns, Sora may be a tool for professionals, not an app for everyone.

slides.hook: Sora's comeback could change how movies get made. Follow to see if the deal closes.
